why: The user correctly pointed out that the earlier "client rejects debugging" conclusion rested on launch failures whose cause had not been isolated, and asked for a controlled re-test of both launch modes before accepting that conclusion.
finding: Both direct launches fail, with different codes: 53 without a debugger and 84 with one. The Steam launch works. So the fast exits are caused by launching the executable directly rather than by debugging.
retraction: My earlier statement that "the client rejects being debugged" is WRONG and is withdrawn. It was inferred from a launch failure that had a different cause. Trial A is specifically decisive: no watchpoint was armed at all, so no breakpoint could have been involved, yet the process still exited with 84.
supporting_history: This also explains earlier inconsistent results: the debugged direct launches that produced 9,209,262 and 37,450,741 debug events show the client can run for a long time under a debugger.
what_remains_open: Whether a hardware watchpoint can be armed on a Steam-launched client early enough to trap the write to Engine.dll+0x421428.
process_note: A control run isolating one variable at a time was the right move here, and I should have done it before drawing the conclusion.

trials.mode: direct CreateProcess WITH DEBUG_ONLY_THIS_PROCESS, no watchpoint armed at all
trials.watch: absolute 0x1, i.e. no valid watch, so no breakpoint was involved
